column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3c, the pedigree of thesis 4 (confidence is a property of the method in the long run); textbook, so use only beside row 2, never alone.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c aha; checked: Morey et al. quote Neyman p.349 'obviously in the negative' and Seidenfeld quotes his zero-or-unity values; after the move Laura's range is the case of unity; say certain, never a percentage.
Mon 16 Nov: store, CONCEIT owner only; a bet against money owned; the conceit is pencil and ink with one turn per part, so this would compete with it.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c, why never '95% confident' for the owned range; textbook; row 7 carries the evidence.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c; the case's question asks for belief about one event (the Bayesian kind), so 3c answers in the case's sense, not as coverage.

Mon 16 Nov: Greenland quote and figures match NUMBERS 4 (house model), but SKELETON 3c gives Table 2 one denominator (joint replay: bottom $80,000-$115,000, top $95,000-$140,000); keep the house spreads in the store, never beside the replays.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, why no percentage label; checked at source: 59%, 55%, mean 3.45, 3% of researchers rejected all six, experience did not predict; sample 118 researchers in the tables (120 took part), 442 first-years and 34 master's students.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c; the correct statement is quoted verbatim in the paper's Materials; supports thesis 4 (her range is the reverse of a confidence interval); one clause at most beside row 7.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c; readers hear 'confident' as belief, so 3c answers how sure the event is; Morey's 'coverage procedure' explains why the label misleads.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c, verified verbatim (lost submarine); a label below certainty on a range known to hold is a mistake; pairs with row 2.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 5 (a probability for one interval needs a prior and is a credible interval); row 5 carries the case link.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c, Keel inference on verified parts; lets 3c say certain without taking sides; say it as certain with the basis, never as 100% coverage (Q4c-026 true by construction, H3-106).

Mon 16 Nov: the ASA line serves 3e (say what the record covers and what it does not); move the IPS's two reasons to 3e, where SKELETON names them once; 3c's confidence sentence carries only the funds' costs beyond the 0.5% cut (Book 19).
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 15 (a future value is not a confidence interval) and of H8-043; row 15 gives NIST's reason.
Mon 16 Nov: Table 2's note and 3c vocabulary; before the move the ends are a prediction, after it nothing is left to predict; why 'confidence interval' is the wrong name.
Mon 16 Nov: CONCEIT owner or 3c bridge; limits set by a rule and held by parts owned, not a statistical interval; a second image beside pencil and ink, so one sentence at most.
Mon 16 Nov: calling the top calibrated and sharp rests on the cap and owned holdings, true by construction (Q4c-026, H3-106); store only, never 'calibrated' in 3c.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c or 3e parallel, verified (sections 2 and 5.1); Basel's level is bank capital over one year against uncertain losses; one clause.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c or 3e; verified; the 0.5% cut pads against what the model cannot see as Basel's 99.9% does; 0.27% and 0.23% match NUMBERS section 0 (l.1921); Basel pads a probability, Laura an amount.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c, state the horizon (bottom from January 2028, top from the move, both to 15 Dec 2032, as NUMBERS); Art. 304 adds to card Q8b.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c or 3e, one clause; verified: GPS 340 paras 15 and 23 (a 75 per cent level of sufficiency, at least central estimate plus half a standard deviation) and APRA 2025 ('75 per cent of the time'); it is the provision for insurance liabilities (claims money), not capital.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e or store; verified (IFRS 17 para 119; ESMA 3.3.6, Talanx 75%, 65%, 83%, 88%); Laura's translation is the record and the exits, not a percentage.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; verified (HM Treasury 3.2.4.8-9, citing IFRS 17's Basis for Conclusions); withdrawn for cost and comparability, not certainty, so the use breaks under its own disanalogy.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c or Table 2's note; verified (S&P paras 127 and 133 and the AAA scenario; the 85% is the Dow); the 1929 case matches NUMBERS 4 Exhibit 3 ($95,000 to $100,000); always say the replay moves US stocks only, rates at forwards.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; UNVERIFIED (search extracts only), so S 2; a weaker twin in spirit of row 24; open both PDFs whole before any use.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of H7-031 (IPCC: confidence is not probabilistic); the added 'distinct from statistical confidence' is row 36's point too.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c or 3e, the basis as several lines that agree; the replays share one engine, so never call them independent lines.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c; one statement of how sure and why, no extra 'very high confidence' label; para 11E adds to Q4c's 11D.
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and 3c, certainty has dates (aha 4): the bottom certain from the January 2028 purchase, before that it rests on the deposit (IPS l.17).
Mon 16 Nov: 3c structure; Wharton's 'level of confidence ... and the factors' maps to ICD 203's likelihood and confidence in the basis; Q4c rows 4-6 hold the scale, not this split.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c first clause; name the outcome, its timing and its nature before how sure, which answers the cold readers' 'confidence about what?'.
Mon 16 Nov: store; a contrast (assurance from samples against Treasuries owned in full); no job a part needs.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c; say what the confidence is before what can stop it, or the statement reads as a hedge.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3d; 'confidence level' calls up a poll's plus-or-minus and its misses; say certain with the basis.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e; a count of tested futures must say what it does not cover; overlaps row 13 and Q4c-026.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, Client Knowledge; lines checked (case l.115, l.116, l.117-118, l.127; FR instructions l.113-114); the case's own three senses explain the cold readers' question, and 3c answers sense 2 by name.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; wordplay with no evidence the case writer meant it; never in the report.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c check, Keel synthesis; extends H9-019 and the aha reserve on the statistics graduate with what she would object to.

Mon 16 Nov: Table 2's note; figures match NUMBERS 4 (92.2%, 59.8%; 2.9%, 6.2%, 8.7%, 10.7%); reword per aha 7: before the move the top is never owned, so say a top named early would turn out larger than the move could buy; the idea is H10-059's.
